chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 80 — Disorder in the Days of Sinners
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. The surviving Aramaic manuscripts of the Astronomical Book do not preserve wording securely corresponding to Chapter 80, and no extant Greek witness preserves it. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is therefore the translation base for all eight verses: Uriel's summary, shortened seasons, delayed fruit, changes in the moon and stars, human error and punishment. The difficult wording in verse 5 is translated as it stands in the extant Geʽez text, including its reference to barrenness at the edge of the western chariot; no conjectural replacement is inserted. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: In those days Uriel answered me and said, “Look, Enoch, I have shown you everything and revealed it all to you, so that you may see this sun and this moon, the leaders of the stars of heaven, and all those who turn them—their work, their appointed times and their departures.”
verses.study: Uriel summarizes the revelation as something Enoch is meant to see and retain. Heavenly movements include leaders, workers, times and departures.
crossReferences: Habakkuk 2:2 — revealed vision is preserved clearly
Revelation 1:19 — the seer writes what has been shown

verses.text: In the days of sinners the rainy seasons will grow short, and their seed will come late in their lands and fields. Every work upon the earth will change and will not appear at its appointed time; rain will be withheld, and heaven will hold it back.
verses.study: Sin is followed by disruption in rain, planting and harvest timing. The earth's altered works expose the cost of moral disorder.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 28:23–24 — disobedience is answered by withheld rain
Jeremiah 14:3–4 — failed rain leaves the land and its workers ashamed

verses.text: In those times the fruit of the earth will come late and will not grow at its appointed time, and the fruit of the trees will be withheld in its season.
verses.study: Delay moves from seed and rain to field and tree fruit. Creation no longer yields according to the expected season.
crossReferences: Leviticus 26:19–20 — land and trees can withhold their produce
Haggai 1:10–11 — heaven and earth withhold dew and crops

verses.text: The moon will change its order and will not appear at its appointed time.
verses.study: The disorder reaches from agriculture into the lunar course. The failure of an expected appearance becomes a sign of wider disruption.
crossReferences: Joel 2:10 — sun and moon grow dark in a day of judgment
Luke 21:25 — signs appear in sun, moon and stars

verses.text: In those days the sky will appear, and barrenness will reach the far edge of the great chariot in the west; it will shine much more brightly than the prescribed order of light.
verses.study: The preserved Geʽez wording joins barrenness at the western chariot with abnormal brightness. The difficult image is retained without replacing it with a smoother conjecture.
crossReferences: Isaiah 24:4–6 — a withered earth accompanies covenant judgment
Isaiah 30:26 — extraordinary brightness can mark a decisive divine day

verses.text: Many heads of the stars will stray from the command. They will change their paths and their work and will not appear at the times appointed for them.
verses.study: The star leaders' failure is defined as departure from command, path, work and time. Cosmic disorder mirrors the sinners' rejection of appointed ways.
crossReferences: Judges 5:20 — stars are pictured as acting from their courses
Jude 13 — wandering stars symbolize reserved judgment

verses.text: The whole order of the stars will be hidden from sinners. The thoughts of those who dwell upon the earth will go astray concerning them; they will turn from all their ways, err, and regard them as gods.
verses.study: Hidden order produces not humility but idolatrous error. When people lose the created pattern, they mistake the lights for gods rather than servants.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:19 — Israel is warned not to worship the heavenly host
Romans 1:25 — creation is worshiped in place of the Creator

verses.text: Evil will multiply against them, and punishment will come upon them to destroy them all.
verses.study: The chapter ends with evil's increase and answering punishment. Persistent corruption reaches a destructive consequence.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:5–7 — multiplied human evil precedes sweeping judgment
Matthew 24:12 — increasing lawlessness causes love to grow cold

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 80 turns from the regular courses of the luminaries to a time when sinners experience disorder in rain, crops, moon and stars. Uriel frames the warning within everything already shown to Enoch.
Shortened rainy seasons and late seed lead to delayed field and tree fruit. Moral rebellion and ecological loss are presented as connected features of judgment.

The moon and star leaders then depart from appointed order. The chapter describes changed appearance, paths, work and timing without asking the reader to correct the ancient vision into a modern astronomical scheme.
Human thought also goes astray. Instead of recognizing the lights as commanded servants, people regard them as gods, and multiplying evil is answered by punishment.

crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:19 — heavenly lights must not be worshiped
Deuteronomy 28:22–24 — drought and failed rain accompany covenant judgment
Isaiah 24:4–6 — sin and curse wither the earth
Joel 2:10 — heavenly lights are disturbed in judgment
Romans 1:21–25 — darkened thought exchanges the Creator for creation
Jude 13 — wandering stars are reserved for darkness
